sourceDesc.p: Authority file compiled from the correspondence of Filippo Cavriana.

p.bibl: Medici Archive Project, MIA (Medici Interactive Archive), https://mia.medici.org. Person identifiers and the dates marked @source="#map-mia" were verified against MAP's biographical records.

Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani, Rome: Istituto della Enciclopedia Italiana, 1960–. Cited by the entry's own identifier, as at https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/. Where the Dizionario and the Medici Archive disagree, the Dizionario is followed, and the other reading recorded in a note on the person.

Wikidata (https://www.wikidata.org) and Wikimedia Commons. Matches were anchored on VIAF where the file holds one, and otherwise accepted only where birth and death years corroborate. Portrait file names refer to Commons; the images are not copied here.

Wikipedia. Used only where a person has no image on their Wikidata item; the article's own illustration was then inspected before use, since an article's lead image is as often a coat of arms or a history painting as a likeness.

calendar.p: The Julian calendar, the reckoning of this edition and of the letters themselves. Dates before the Gregorian reform of October 1582 are given in it, and are marked with @when-custom; the @when beside them holds the proleptic Gregorian equivalent, ten days later, which is what that attribute means in TEI. Dates after the reform are already Gregorian and carry @when alone.

The Florentine year, ab Incarnatione, which began on 25 March. A day between 1 January and 24 March therefore carries a year one lower than ours, and only those days differ: the rest of the year agrees. Dates marked with this method are given as their source prints them, unconverted.

revisionDesc.change: "Messer Alberto segretario", who confirmed Concino's goodwill to Cavriana by word of mouth in the letter of 15 July 1570, identified as probable Alberto Luchi, MAP 18680. He is the only Alberto in the Medici Archive holding a secretaryship, and the ducal payroll of 1 March 1567 puts him in Concino's own chancery, six scudi, in the same run of secretaries as Iacopo Dani, whom the letter names. Recorded with cert="medium": the letter offers a forename and an office and nothing more.

Alamanni's dates marked datingMethod="#florentine" and a Florentine calendar declared. The Dizionario's 13 March 1536 and January 1590 both fall in the span where the Florentine year runs behind ours, and the file had been asserting them as though they were ours. They stand as the Dizionario prints them; in common style they are 1537 and 1591.

Vincenzo Alamanni's dates taken from the Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani (Clementina Rotondi, vol. 1, 1960), which gives 13 March 1536 and January 1590 against the Medici Archive's 1537 and 1591. The Dizionario is the fuller witness — it names the place of birth and death and the cause — and is followed here. The discrepancy is not random: both its dates fall in the span where the Florentine year runs one behind ours, and MAP's are exactly their common-style equivalents. The point is recorded on the person rather than settled silently.

Alessandro Striggio matched to MAP 892 (1537-1592), the composer, not MAP 3228, which is his son Sandrino (1572-1630). He had been missed because his birth year was recorded only in @when with no text content, so the generated data showed him as undated and the date guard had nothing to separate father from son.

The earlier MAP reconciliation had searched only the Florentine and Mantuan functionaries, leaving the French principals unmatched — which made the archive look as though it did not hold Coligny, Guise or the Cardinal of Lorraine. It does. Every remaining person was searched, and 22 more matched where MAP's birth and death years corroborate our own.

MAP's offices carry start and end years, so they are now recorded with @from and @to. A reader can be told what a man held at the moment a letter names him rather than what he became: Vincenzo Alamanni is inviato mediceo in Francia from 1568 and ambasciatore only from 1572.

pers-sanseverino-g merged into pers-galeazzosanseverino-g. The letters call him "conte di Gaiazzo" and "Gaiazzo", and MAP 19477 gives Gian Galeazzo Sanseverino di Aragona the title Conte di Caiazzo, so the two records were one man. Offices, dates and index names for the 39 people carrying a MAP identifier were taken from MAP's biographical records, restricted to posts held between 1566 and 1574.

pers-lorraine-h1 merged into pers-guise-h: both records described Henri I de Lorraine, duke of Guise, and both resolved to the same Wikidata item and the same portrait. The one reference the duplicate held, a bare "Loreno" in the letter of 14 January 1571, was repointed to the Cardinal of Lorraine, which is what bare "Loreno" denotes elsewhere in this corpus. The duplicate's VIAF id was kept, being the one Wikidata records for the duke.

Twenty-eight people identified who had previously gone unmatched. The earlier pass required birth and death years to corroborate, which no record lacking dates could ever satisfy; these were matched instead on the name together with the title the file records, and each was required to have been alive while the letters were written.

Alfonso d'Este corrected: the record carried MAP 2970 and Q1616509, both of which are Alfonso d'Este of Montecchio (1527-1587) rather than Alfonso II, Duke of Ferrara (1533-1597). Este Cardinal identified as Luigi d'Este, the duke's brother, on the evidence of the letter of 1 September 1570.

Removed four VIAF identifiers that resolved to a different person: Emanuele Filiberto di Savoia, François de Valois, Johann Casimir von der Pfalz and Filippo Strozzi. Each was checked against Wikidata, and for the first two the Medici Archive Project's dates corroborate the error. The identifiers for Zygmunt II and Katarzyna were kept: they resolve to Sigismund II Augustus and Catherine of Austria, the same people under different name forms.

person.note: The Medici Archive gives 1537 and 1591. Both of the Dizionario's dates fall between 1 January and 24 March, the span in which the Florentine year, beginning on 25 March, runs one behind ours, and MAP's years are exactly what those dates yield when converted to common style. That MAP converts silently is demonstrable: its record of the household payroll of Mediceo del Principato 616, f. 271r, a document of 1 March, heads it 1567 while its own detail carries the archival 1566. Whether Rotondi reports the Florentine reckoning of her sources or had already converted it the article does not say; this edition follows the Dizionario as printed and marks the dates Florentine, so that in common style they are to be read as 1537 and 1591.

person.note: Probably Alberto Luchi, whom the Medici Archive records as Alberto Luci, a secretary in the Medici chancery. The payroll of the ducal household of 1 March 1567 — Mediceo del Principato 616, f. 271r — lists him at six scudi among the secretaries of Cosimo I, after Belisario Vinta and before Bernardino Grazini, under messer Bartolomeo Concini, who is the man this letter is written to, and in the same run as messer Iacopo Dani, whom the same paragraph of the letter names as the writer's friend. He was still in Medici service in 1572, when Orazio Urbani wrote to him from Venice about silks ordered by the Grand Duchess. He is the only person in the archive whose given name is Alberto and whose recorded office is a secretaryship. The identification is offered as probable, not certain: the letter gives a forename and an office and nothing else, so it rests on the milieu rather than on the name.
